conclusions: Element 13 failures no longer consist only of cached selectors: 230 additional failures explicitly contain the edited XPath, across 14 campaigns. 57 additional failures still contain the old XPath.

The five largest group-post failure counts are 37702=57, 43257=30, 43258=30, 43259=27, 43260=22. Several runs attempt many position indexes; seeding campaign 42111 includes failures at positions 50 through 130. Without DOM/match counts this does not prove why those indexes were missing.
Like outcomes now exist: element 1691 reported 178 liked=true and four missing-button results; element 1132 reported four new Likes with alreadyLiked=false.

Element 1692 reported 20 successful openings followed by 20 focus and submit successes. Eleven missing-button failures occur at opening; downstream focused/commented=false should not be counted as eleven additional textbox/submit failures.
Newsfeed missing-button logs do not include the resolved XPath, so old/new cached-selector version cannot be determined for those failed steps.
Element 1517 timeouts do not alone prove that its XPath is wrong or that the dialog opened. No selector/screenshot events were available for the inspected newsfeed and campaign46363 runs.
All five edited element rows still contain the requested XPath with unchanged edit timestamps.
